article.title: Japanese Town Wants Limits on Smartphone Use
paragraphs: The town of Toyoake in Japan is proposing a plan to limit smartphone usage for its 69,000 residents to just two hours a day! This idea is being discussed by the local lawmakers after being suggested by Mayor Masafumi Koki. He explained that the limit won’t be enforced strictly; it’s meant to help families think about how much time they spend on devices. “The two-hour limit... is merely a guideline... to encourage citizens,” he said.

This plan, if approved in October, won’t apply to work or school activities, like online learning or exercising while listening to music. Many residents are sharing their thoughts, and about 80% of feedback during a consultation period was against the proposal.

Some people worry that two hours isn’t enough for activities like reading or watching a movie. The mayor recognizes that while smartphones are useful, they can also lead to students missing school or families spending less time together.

languageFocus.title: Language Focus
languageFocus.topic: Target Structures: Modal & Negative Forms, Passive Voice, Reported Speech, Purpose, Contrast with While, Cause/Effect & Quantity Expressions

languagePatterns.pattern: 1. Negative & Modal Auxiliary Forms (won’t / isn’t / can)
languagePatterns.explanation: Use contracted modal auxiliaries ('won’t apply', 'won’t be enforced') and negative copulas ('isn’t enough') to specify official boundaries, exemptions, and perceived limitations.
languagePatterns.example: The advisory code won’t impose legal penalties, but critics insist three hours isn’t sufficient for research.
languagePatterns.sourceExample: He explained that the limit won’t be enforced strictly... won’t apply to work or school activities... isn’t enough...

languagePatterns.pattern: 2. Present Passive Voice (is being discussed / after being suggested)
languagePatterns.explanation: Use present progressive and prepositional passive constructions to describe policy measures currently undergoing democratic review.
languagePatterns.example: The proposed traffic reduction plan is currently being discussed by the municipal council.
languagePatterns.sourceExample: This idea is being discussed by the local lawmakers after being suggested by Mayor Masafumi Koki.

languagePatterns.pattern: 3. Reported Speech & Attribution Verbs (explained that / recognizes that / said)
languagePatterns.explanation: Attribute policy rationale and institutional positions clearly using reporting verbs followed by complement clauses or direct speech.
languagePatterns.example: The superintendent explained that the recommendation was designed to foster independent study habits.
languagePatterns.sourceExample: He explained that the limit won’t be enforced strictly... “The two-hour limit... is merely a guideline,” he said.

languagePatterns.pattern: 4. Purpose & Intended Function (meant to / to encourage / to help)
languagePatterns.explanation: Clarify the educational and social aims of a public policy using passive purpose adjectives ('is meant to') and infinitive phrases.
languagePatterns.example: The municipal guidelines are meant to encourage healthy lifestyle reflection rather than mandate behavior.
languagePatterns.sourceExample: ...it’s meant to help families think about how much time they spend on devices. “...merely a guideline... to encourage citizens...”

languagePatterns.pattern: 5. Concessive Contrast with 'While' (while smartphones are useful, they can also...)
languagePatterns.explanation: Structure nuanced, balanced claims by admitting an acknowledged advantage in a subordinate clause before presenting an accompanying concern in the main clause.
languagePatterns.example: While digital screens are essential for modern coursework, they can also disrupt nocturnal rest.
languagePatterns.sourceExample: The mayor recognizes that while smartphones are useful, they can also lead to students missing school...

languagePatterns.pattern: 6. Cause/Effect & Quantity Expressions (lead to / about 80% / just two hours)
languagePatterns.explanation: Link screen behaviors to social outcomes using causal phrasal verbs ('lead to') while citing precise quantitative metrics ('69,000 residents', 'about 80% of feedback').
languagePatterns.example: Unregulated evening device usage can lead to classroom fatigue, prompting about 70% of educators to express concern.
languagePatterns.sourceExample: ...limit smartphone usage for its 69,000 residents to just two hours a day... about 80% of feedback... lead to students missing school...

teacherNotes.note: The article is an informational current-affairs report credited to 'Source: The Guardian' titled 'Japanese Town Wants Limits on Smartphone Use.' It explores municipal governance and digital wellness in modern Japan, focusing on how a local government attempts to influence citizens' private technology habits through non-punitive public policy.

Toyoake is a real municipality in Aichi Prefecture, Japan, with approximately 69,000 residents. Emphasize to students that this is a municipal (town-level) initiative rather than a nationwide Japanese law, demonstrating how local governments often experiment with community wellness guidelines.

The policy was suggested by Mayor Masafumi Koki and submitted to local lawmakers for deliberation. Guide students to recognize the administrative chain: a mayor proposes an initiative, and municipal legislators debate its adoption on behalf of the community.

The suggested threshold is 'just two hours a day.' Help students conceptualize this duration: for teenagers accustomed to multiple hours of social media, streaming, and gaming, a two-hour total represents a significant behavioural contraction.

A central textual nuance is that the limit 'won’t be enforced strictly' and is 'merely a guideline... to encourage citizens.' There are no police checks, software trackers, or monetary fines. Its primary purpose is moral suasion and behavioural nudge, encouraging families to reflect on screen time.

teacherNotes.topic: 6. Practical Exemptions for School, Work, and Exercise
teacherNotes.note: Paragraph 2 clarifies that the proposal will not apply to work or school activities, including online learning or exercising while listening to music. This demonstrates policy practicality: officials distinguish between productive/educational screen time and passive entertainment.

teacherNotes.topic: 7. The October Timeline and Democratic Process
teacherNotes.note: The text notes: 'This plan, if approved in October...' This conditional phrasing ('if approved') signals ongoing legislative deliberation rather than an already finalized or implemented statute.

teacherNotes.topic: 8. Consultation Period and the 80% Opposition Feedback
teacherNotes.note: During a formal public consultation period, about 80% of submitted feedback was against the proposal. Highlight this striking statistic: it shows a vibrant democratic feedback mechanism where four out of five participating citizens actively pushed back against municipal intrusion into private daily routines.

teacherNotes.topic: 9. Resident Arguments: Reading and Watching Movies
teacherNotes.note: Residents specifically argue that two hours is insufficient for culturally enriching or relaxing pastimes like reading digital books or watching a full-length feature film. This illustrates how digital screens now combine essential cultural consumption with casual browsing.

teacherNotes.topic: 10. The Mayor's Duality: Usefulness versus Social Hazards
teacherNotes.note: Paragraph 3 highlights the mayor's nuanced perspective: he explicitly recognizes that smartphones are useful tools, yet warns they can lead to students missing school (school absenteeism/truancy) and families spending less time communicating together.

teacherNotes.topic: 11. Disciplinary Literacy: Guideline versus Legal Mandate
teacherNotes.note: Teach students to distinguish carefully between an unenforced advisory guideline (moral suasion) and a punitive statutory ban. Many ESL students conflate any government announcement with a criminal law enforced by police; correcting this distinction is essential.

teacherNotes.topic: 12. Strict Factual Scope and Avoiding Outside Extrapolation
teacherNotes.note: Caution students against importing outside legal cases (such as Kagawa Prefecture's gaming ordinance), medical screen-time guidelines from the WHO, or invented Japanese constitutional controversies. All writing must be strictly grounded in the 164 words of Source F.

Source F is an isolated study of digital wellness in Unit 5 (Technology, Society & Well-Being). Do not cross-reference AI music (Source E), colonialism in Singapore or Congo (Sources C and D), or earlier environmental units.

teacherNotes.topic: 14. ESL Scaffolding for G1 and G2 Learners
teacherNotes.note: For G1 learners, scaffold the debate using a clear binary frame: 'Mayor's Intent (family reflection, less missed school) vs. Resident Resistance (80% against, reading/movies need time)'. For G2 learners, demand sophisticated concession syntax using 'while', 'even though', and precise nominalizations like 'consultation feedback'.

teachingScript.objective: Engage students with the concept of a government setting a two-hour smartphone guideline and introduce Source F from The Guardian.
teachingScript.scriptEn: Good morning, class! Imagine your local mayor announcing that everyone in your town should limit their smartphone use to just two hours a day! How would you react? Today we explore Source F from The Guardian, which takes us to the town of Toyoake in Japan. We will examine why Mayor Masafumi Koki proposed this two-hour guideline, how 80% of residents reacted, and how communities grapple with the balance between useful technology and family well-being.
teachingScript.scriptKo: 좋은 아침입니다, 여러분! 여러분이 사는 동네의 시장님이 모든 주민에게 하루 스마트폰 사용을 딱 2시간으로 제한하라고 발표한다고 상상해 보세요! 여러분은 어떻게 반응하시겠습니까? 오늘 우리는 The Guardian의 Source F를 통해 일본의 도요아케시로 가봅니다. 고키 마사후미 시장이 왜 이 2시간 지침을 제안했는지, 주민의 80%가 어떻게 반응했는지, 그리고 현대 사회가 유용한 기술과 가족의 안녕 사이에서 어떻게 균형을 잡으려 하는지 함께 살펴볼 것입니다.
teachingScript.studentActions: Open the lesson app, read the lesson title and goal, and prepare their notebooks for analytical discussion.
teachingScript.misconceptionFeedback: Clarify that the proposed policy is an advisory guideline to encourage reflection, not a criminal law enforced by police fines.
teachingScript.transition: Let us begin with our Warm-up questions to examine our own screen habits and the purpose of public guidelines.

teachingScript.objective: Activate prior knowledge regarding daily screen time, guidelines versus strict laws, and balancing digital benefits with family life.
teachingScript.scriptEn: Turn to your partner and examine our three Warm-up questions. Question 1 asks about your typical daily screen routine. Question 2 contrasts a voluntary guideline with a strictly enforced rule. Question 3 asks how communities can balance the undeniable benefits of digital devices with family time and student attendance. Use our sentence starters to frame your answers.
teachingScript.scriptKo: 짝과 함께 3가지 워밍업 질문을 살펴보세요. 1번 질문은 여러분의 일상적인 화면 사용 시간에 대해 묻습니다. 2번 질문은 자율적인 가이드라인과 엄격하게 집행되는 규칙의 차이를 대조합니다. 3번 질문은 디지털 기기의 명백한 이점과 가족 간의 시간 및 출석 문제 사이에서 공동체가 어떻게 균형을 맞출 수 있는지 묻습니다. 문장 시작 표현을 활용하여 답변을 구성해 보세요.
teachingScript.studentActions: Discuss each question in pairs, write short responses using the provided sentence starters, and share viewpoints with the class.
teachingScript.misconceptionFeedback: Remind students that public health or community guidelines rely on awareness rather than punitive coercion.
teachingScript.transition: Now let us turn to the authentic text of Source F to see exactly what Toyoake is proposing.

teachingScript.objective: Perform close reading of Source F, verifying paragraph boundaries, factual details, and exact quotations.
teachingScript.scriptEn: Let us read Source F together. Follow along carefully as we read the headline and three paragraphs. Notice that Paragraph 1 establishes the town, the 69,000 residents, the two-hour limit, and Mayor Koki's emphasis that this is merely an unenforced guideline. Paragraph 2 highlights work and school exemptions and the 80% opposition in consultation feedback. Paragraph 3 contrasts resident worries about movies and reading with the mayor's concerns about missing school and family time.
teachingScript.scriptKo: Source F를 함께 읽어보겠습니다. 제목과 3개 단락을 주의 깊게 따라와 주세요. 1단락은 도요아케시, 69,000명의 주민, 2시간 제한, 그리고 이것이 강제 집행되지 않는 단순한 가이드라인이라는 고키 시장의 설명을 제시합니다. 2단락은 직장과 학교 활동의 예외 적용과 의견 수렴에서 나타난 80%의 반대 의견을 다룹니다. 3단락은 영화와 독서에 대한 주민들의 우려와 결석 및 가족 시간에 대한 시장의 우려를 대조합니다.
teachingScript.studentActions: Track the reading, underline key figures (69,000, two hours, 80%), and highlight the mayor's direct quotes.
teachingScript.misconceptionFeedback: Emphasize that the ellipses '...' inside the quote are original textual punctuation, not sentence breaks.
teachingScript.transition: With the text clearly understood, let us master the 10 essential vocabulary terms in context.

teachingScript.objective: Master 10 academic and civic terms from Source F, connecting English definitions, Korean meanings, and context examples.
teachingScript.scriptEn: Examine our 10 vocabulary terms: propose, smartphone usage, enforce strictly, guideline, residents, lawmakers, consultation period, feedback, against the proposal, and spend time together. Notice how 'guideline' contrasts with 'enforce strictly', and how 'consultation period' provides the setting where 80% of feedback was 'against the proposal'.
teachingScript.scriptKo: 10개의 어휘를 살펴봅시다: propose(제안하다), smartphone usage(스마트폰 사용량), enforce strictly(엄격히 집행하다), guideline(지침), residents(주민들), lawmakers(지방의원들), consultation period(의견 수렴 기간), feedback(의견/피드백), against the proposal(제안에 반대하는), spend time together(함께 시간을 보내다). 'guideline'이 'enforce strictly'와 어떻게 대조되는지, 그리고 'consultation period' 동안 80%의 피드백이 어떻게 'against the proposal'이었는지 확인하세요.
teachingScript.studentActions: Read each term, pronounce it aloud, review the Korean definition and example sentence, and record notes.
teachingScript.misconceptionFeedback: Ensure students understand that 'against the proposal' functions as a prepositional phrase expressing direct disagreement.
teachingScript.transition: Let us now verify our factual comprehension through the Main Idea question and the 6 Reading Comprehension items.

teachingScript.objective: Evaluate understanding of the central thesis and verify 6 factual items with immediate O/X feedback and paragraph citations.
teachingScript.scriptEn: First, complete the Main Idea question. Look for the balanced answer that mentions both the non-strict two-hour guideline and the competing perspectives. Next, answer the 6 Reading Comprehension questions. For each question, eliminate distractors that invent fines or outside laws, and verify your answer against the exact sentence in Paragraphs 1, 2, or 3.
teachingScript.scriptKo: 먼저 주제(Main Idea) 문제를 풀어보세요. 강제 집행되지 않는 2시간 지침과 상충하는 관점들을 모두 담고 있는 균형 잡힌 보기를 찾으세요. 이어서 6개의 독해 확인 문제를 풉니다. 벌금이나 외부 법률을 날조한 오답들을 배제하고, 1, 2, 3단락의 정확한 문장과 일치하는지 대조해 보세요.
teachingScript.studentActions: Select answers for the Main Idea and 6 Comprehension MCQs, read the O/X explanations, and note textual references.
teachingScript.misconceptionFeedback: Warn students against choosing options that claim phones will be confiscated or that the guideline is a criminal law.
teachingScript.transition: Now let us practice extracting and synthesizing direct textual evidence in the Evidence from Text section.

teachingScript.objective: Synthesize textual facts to answer 3 structured prompts, utilizing model comparisons to refine completeness.
teachingScript.scriptEn: In the Evidence section, answer our three prompts. Prompt 1 asks what Toyoake is proposing and why Mayor Koki stresses it is an unenforced guideline. Prompt 2 asks about the exemptions and consultation feedback. Prompt 3 explores the balance between smartphone usefulness and social hazards. Write your answer, check the word count, and click 'Compare with Model' to evaluate your work.
teachingScript.scriptKo: 본문 근거 제시 섹션의 3개 질문에 답해 보세요. 1번은 도요아케시의 제안 내용과 고키 시장이 비강제 지침임을 강조한 이유를 묻습니다. 2번은 예외 조항과 의견 수렴 결과를 묻습니다. 3번은 스마트폰의 유용성과 사회적 위험 사이의 균형을 다룹니다. 답안을 작성한 후 '모범 답안과 비교' 버튼을 눌러 점검하세요.
teachingScript.studentActions: Draft written responses in the textareas, monitor word counts, reveal model answers, and self-assess against compare tips.
teachingScript.misconceptionFeedback: Ensure students explicitly include the work/school exemptions in Prompt 2 and both reading/movies and missed school in Prompt 3.
teachingScript.transition: Let us examine our Language Focus structures before applying them in writing practice.

teachingScript.phase: 7. Language Focus, Writing Practice & Final Task (18 mins)
teachingScript.objective: Apply target structures (modals, passive, reported speech, purpose, while, cause/effect) in 4 practice prompts and draft the final 100–140 word paragraph.
teachingScript.scriptEn: Review our Language Focus patterns: modal negatives like 'won’t be enforced strictly', passives like 'is being discussed', reporting frames like 'he explained that', and concessive clauses with 'while'. Complete Writing Practice prompts 1 to 4. Then tackle our Final Writing Task: explain why Toyoake's smartphone guideline is controversial in 100 to 140 words. Include 3 text details, the voluntary guideline, opposing viewpoints, and cause/effect language.
teachingScript.scriptKo: 'won’t be enforced strictly'와 같은 조동사 부정형, 'is being discussed' 같은 수동태, 'he explained that' 같은 전달 표현, 그리고 'while'을 활용한 양보 구문 등 언어 집중 패턴을 복습하세요. 쓰기 연습 1~4번을 완료한 후 최종 과제에 도전합니다: 도요아케시의 스마트폰 지침이 왜 논란이 되는지 100~140단어로 서술하세요. 본문의 구체적 근거 3개, 자율 지침의 성격, 상반된 관점, 그리고 인과 언어가 반드시 포함되어야 합니다.
teachingScript.studentActions: Complete the 4 writing practice exercises, draft the final paragraph, run the rule-based check, and verify the 100–140 word parameter.
teachingScript.misconceptionFeedback: Ensure students stay strictly between 100 and 140 words and present both the 80% resident opposition and the mayor's rationale.
teachingScript.transition: Finally, verify your work against the six Self-Check criteria before submitting your paragraph.

teachingScript.objective: Complete the 6 Self-Check validation items, review draft metrics, and submit final work.
teachingScript.scriptEn: Check off each of the 6 Self-Check items. Did you base your writing strictly on Source F? Did you explain that the guideline is not strictly enforced? Did you cite 69,000 residents, the October timeline, or the 80% feedback? Is your word count strictly between 100 and 140 words? When all six boxes are checked, click Submit. Excellent civic analysis and academic writing today, Grade 9 scholars!
teachingScript.scriptKo: 6개의 자체 점검 기준을 하나씩 확인하며 체크하세요. 철저히 Source F에만 근거했나요? 지침이 엄격하게 강제 집행되지 않는다는 점을 설명했나요? 69,000명의 주민, 10월 승인 시점, 또는 80%의 피드백을 인용했나요? 단어 수가 정확히 100~140단어 사이인가요? 6개 항목을 모두 점검했다면 제출 버튼을 누르세요. 오늘 여러분 모두 훌륭한 시민적 분석과 학술적 글쓰기를 완성했습니다, 9학년 여러분!
teachingScript.studentActions: Check all 6 Self-Check items, submit work, verify local storage status, and conclude the lesson.
teachingScript.misconceptionFeedback: Ensure no student submits before confirming their draft meets the strict 100–140 word parameter.
teachingScript.transition: Dismiss class and prepare teacher review based on the analytical writing rubric.

teachersOpeningScript.option: Option 1: The Two-Hour Device Guideline Hook
teachersOpeningScript.english: Good morning, scholars. / Imagine unlocking your phone right now / and seeing a message from your local town hall: / 'Please limit your smartphone use to just two hours a day.' / How would you feel? / Would you support it as a healthy community reminder, / or would you reject it as government overreach? / Today we visit the town of Toyoake in Japan, / where Mayor Masafumi Koki proposed this exact guideline / for 69,000 residents. / We will discover how 80% of citizens pushed back, / and why balancing digital convenience with family well-being / has ignited an intense municipal debate.
teachersOpeningScript.directKorean: 좋은 아침입니다, 학생 여러분. / 지금 당장 스마트폰을 잠금 해제했을 때 / 지역 구청에서 보낸 이런 메시지를 본다고 상상해 보세요: / '스마트폰 사용을 하루 딱 2시간으로 제한해 주십시오.' / 여러분은 어떤 기분이 들까요? / 건강한 공동체를 위한 조언으로 지지하시겠습니까, / 아니면 정부의 지나친 간섭이라며 거부하시겠습니까? / 오늘 우리는 일본의 도요아케시를 방문합니다, / 그곳에서 고키 마사후미 시장이 바로 이 지침을 제안했습니다 / 69,000명의 주민들을 위해. / 우리는 주민의 80%가 어떻게 반대했는지, / 그리고 디지털 편의성과 가족의 안녕 사이에서 균형을 잡는 일이 / 왜 치열한 지역적 논쟁을 촉발했는지 알아볼 것입니다.
teachersOpeningScript.naturalKorean: 좋은 아침입니다, 여러분. 지금 스마트폰을 켰을 때 구청에서 '하루 스마트폰 사용을 2시간으로 제한해 주세요'라는 알림이 와 있다면 어떤 기분이 들까요? 건강한 생활을 돕는 좋은 조언이라며 반길까요, 아니면 사생활에 대한 지나친 간섭이라며 불만을 느낄까요? 오늘 우리는 일본의 도요아케시로 가봅니다. 고키 마사후미 시장이 69,000명의 주민을 위해 바로 이 2시간 지침을 제안했기 때문입니다. 주민의 무려 80%가 왜 반대 의견을 냈는지, 유용한 디지털 기기와 소중한 가족 시간 사이에서 어떤 치열한 고민이 오갔는지 함께 살펴보겠습니다.
teachersOpeningScript.purpose: Hooks student interest through an immediate personal scenario of receiving a municipal screen-time limit.

teachersOpeningScript.option: Option 2: Critical Disciplinary & Civic Policy Hook
teachersOpeningScript.english: Welcome, class. / In Grade 9 academic English, / we evaluate public policies / through careful, evidence-based inquiry. / When local governments address technology habits, / a crucial distinction arises: / is the policy an enforceable legal mandate, / or is it merely an advisory guideline / meant to encourage reflection? / In Source F from The Guardian, / we examine Mayor Koki's proposal in Toyoake, Japan. / We will analyze why exemptions for school and work were included, / why 80% of consultation feedback opposed the measure, / and how municipal leaders balance digital utility against social well-being. / Our goal today / is to write a rigorous analytical paragraph / capturing both sides of this controversy.
teachersOpeningScript.directKorean: 환영합니다, 학생 여러분. / 9학년 학술 영어 수업에서, / 우리는 공공 정책을 평가합니다 / 신중하고 근거 중심의 탐구를 통해. / 지방 정부가 기술 사용 습관을 다룰 때, / 결정적인 차이점이 발생합니다: / 그 정책이 강제 집행 가능한 법적 명령인가, / 아니면 단순한 자율적 지침인가 / 성찰을 독려하기 위한? / The Guardian의 Source F에서, / 우리는 일본 도요아케시 고키 시장의 제안을 검토합니다. / 우리는 왜 학교와 직장 활동에 예외가 포함되었는지, / 왜 의견 수렴 피드백의 80%가 이 조치에 반대했는지, / 그리고 지자체 지도자들이 디지털 유용성과 사회적 안녕 사이에서 어떻게 균형을 잡는지 분석할 것입니다. / 오늘 우리의 목표는 / 엄격하고 분석적인 단락을 작성하는 것입니다 / 이 논란의 양면을 모두 포착해 내는.
teachersOpeningScript.naturalKorean: 환영합니다, 여러분. 9학년 학술 영어 수업에서는 공공 정책을 근거 중심으로 엄밀하게 분석합니다. 지자체가 시민들의 기술 습관에 개입할 때 반드시 짚어야 할 핵심 질문이 있습니다. 바로 이 정책이 벌금을 동반한 강제 법안인지, 아니면 시민 스스로 생각해보게 하는 자율적 권고 지침인지의 여부입니다. The Guardian의 Source F를 통해 우리는 일본 도요아케시의 사례를 살펴봅니다. 학업과 업무 예외 조항에도 불구하고 왜 주민의 80%가 반대했는지, 그리고 시장은 왜 여전히 결석과 가족 소통 단절을 우려하는지 분석하며, 이 논쟁의 양면을 균형 있게 다루는 학술 글쓰기를 완성해 봅시다.
teachersOpeningScript.purpose: Focuses on civic literacy, distinguishing advisory guidelines from statutory mandates, and evaluating public consultation data.

teachersOpeningScript.english: Hello, everyone. / Look at the central tension in Unit 5: / technology brings incredible power to read, learn, and communicate, / yet it can also pull us away from classrooms and family conversations. / Mayor Masafumi Koki recognized this exact dilemma: / smartphones are useful, / but they can also lead to students missing school / and families spending less time together. / When Toyoake proposed a two-hour guideline, / residents asked: Is two hours enough for a movie or a book? / Today we will master the language of cause, effect, and contrast / so you can explain why this simple guideline / became one of the most talked-about civic debates in Japan.
teachersOpeningScript.directKorean: 안녕하세요, 여러분. / 5단원의 핵심적인 긴장을 보세요: / 기술은 읽고, 배우고, 소통하는 놀라운 힘을 가져오지만, / 동시에 우리를 교실과 가족 간의 대화로부터 멀어지게 만들 수도 있습니다. / 고키 마사후미 시장은 이 정확한 딜레마를 인식했습니다: / 스마트폰은 유용하지만, / 학생들이 학교를 결석하게 만들고 / 가족들이 함께 보내는 시간을 줄어들게 할 수도 있다고. / 도요아케시가 2시간 지침을 제안했을 때, / 주민들은 물었습니다: 2시간이 영화 한 편이나 책 한 권 보기에 충분한가? / 오늘 우리는 원인, 결과, 대조의 언어를 마스터할 것입니다 / 여러분이 왜 이 단순한 지침이 / 일본에서 가장 뜨겁게 논의된 시민적 논쟁 중 하나가 되었는지 설명할 수 있도록.
teachersOpeningScript.naturalKorean: 안녕하세요, 여러분. 5단원의 핵심 주제를 생각해 봅시다. 디지털 기술은 우리에게 끝없는 학습과 소통의 기회를 주지만, 동시에 교실 출석을 방해하고 가족과의 소중한 대화를 앗아가기도 합니다. 고키 마사후미 시장 역시 이 딜레마를 잘 알고 있었습니다. 스마트폰이 매우 유용하지만, 학생들의 결석을 유발하고 가족이 함께하는 시간을 줄일 수 있다는 점을 인정한 것입니다. 반면 주민들은 2시간이 영화를 보거나 독서를 하기에 턱없이 부족하다고 호소했습니다. 오늘 우리는 원인과 결과, 대조를 나타내는 정확한 영어 표현을 익혀 이 흥미로운 논쟁을 멋진 학술 단락으로 서술해 볼 것입니다.
teachersOpeningScript.purpose: Connects directly to the Unit 5 overarching theme of technology, society, and well-being.

q1.focus: Personal Screen Routines and Daily Digital Habits
q1.teacherTalk: Encourage students to estimate their actual daily device hours honestly. Ask: Between messaging friends, listening to music, watching videos, studying online, and gaming, how many hours do you realistically accumulate? Point out that many people are surprised to discover their daily screen time easily exceeds four to six hours, which helps them appreciate why a two-hour limit would feel very restrictive.
q1.sampleStudentAnswer: On a typical day, I usually spend about four to five hours on screen devices, mainly for watching videos, texting classmates, and completing homework assignments.
q1.followUpQuestion: If you were asked to cut your non-school device time down to just two hours today, what specific digital activity would you sacrifice first?

q2.focus: Advisory Guidelines versus Enforceable Legal Rules
q2.teacherTalk: Clarify the civic and legal distinction between advisory standards and mandatory statutes. An enforceable rule carries legal authority, monitoring mechanisms, and penalties (like traffic tickets or school detentions). A guideline, like Toyoake's, is an educational recommendation designed to prompt self-reflection and social mindfulness without punishment.
q2.sampleStudentAnswer: While a strict legal rule requires compliance through official penalties like fines, a voluntary public guideline focuses on raising awareness and helping citizens voluntarily rethink their habits.
q2.followUpQuestion: Do you think voluntary guidelines are effective at changing human habits, or do people simply ignore recommendations that lack penalties?

q3.focus: Balancing Digital Benefits with Social and Educational Well-Being
q3.teacherTalk: Guide students to examine trade-offs. Digital devices provide indispensable educational resources, exercise motivation through music, and global knowledge. However, unregulated usage can erode family interactions, disrupt sleep, and lead to school absenteeism. Emphasize that finding balance requires setting intentional boundaries rather than imposing blanket bans.
q3.sampleStudentAnswer: Communities can balance technology benefits with social well-being by creating practical exemptions for education and exercise while encouraging families to establish screen-free mealtimes and bedtime routines.
q3.followUpQuestion: Why did Mayor Koki specifically choose to exempt online learning and exercise music from the proposed two-hour smartphone limit?

koreanEslErrorPairs.error: Toyoake police will arrest all 69,000 residents if they touch phone over two hours.
koreanEslErrorPairs.correction: Mayor Masafumi Koki explained that the two-hour limit won’t be enforced strictly, as it is merely an advisory guideline meant to encourage families to reflect on screen time.
koreanEslErrorPairs.explanation: Korean ESL students frequently confuse local advisory guidelines with criminal laws. The text explicitly states the limit 'won’t be enforced strictly' and is 'merely a guideline'—there are no police arrests or legal fines.

koreanEslErrorPairs.error: The plan bans online learning and exercise music in October.
koreanEslErrorPairs.correction: If approved in October, the plan won’t apply to work or school activities, like online learning or exercising while listening to music.
koreanEslErrorPairs.explanation: Watch out for negative auxiliary meaning: 'won’t apply to' means those activities are exempted from the limit, not that they are banned.

koreanEslErrorPairs.error: All people in Japan voted 80% against smartphones forever.
koreanEslErrorPairs.correction: About 80% of feedback during Toyoake's local consultation period was against the two-hour guideline proposal.
koreanEslErrorPairs.explanation: Do not generalize local consultation feedback to an entire nation or an absolute ban on phones; the 80% opposition was specific to the feedback submitted during Toyoake's consultation period.

koreanEslErrorPairs.error: Mayor Koki hates smartphones and says they have zero use for students.
koreanEslErrorPairs.correction: The mayor recognizes that while smartphones are useful, they can also lead to students missing school or families spending less time together.

teachingTranscript.korean: 3번 문장의 세미콜론을 보세요. 시장은 두 가지 핵심을 명확히 합니다: 첫째, 엄격히 강제되지 않을 것이며, 둘째, 가족의 성찰을 돕기 위한 취지라는 점입니다.

sentenceAnalysis.directKorean: 많은 주민들이 자신들의 생각을 나누고 있으며, / 약 80%의 피드백이 / 의견 수렴 기간 동안의 / 그 제안에 반대했습니다.
sentenceAnalysis.naturalKorean: 많은 주민들이 의견을 활발히 나누고 있는 가운데, 의견 수렴 기간 동안 접수된 피드백의 약 80%가 이 제안에 반대하는 입장이었습니다.

mustKnowChunks.use: idiomatic present continuous phrase describing public civic participation
mustKnowChunks.example: Citizens attended the town hall, actively sharing their thoughts on property zoning.

mustKnowChunks.use: temporal prepositional phrase identifying an official public engagement window
mustKnowChunks.example: Over five hundred letters were received during a consultation period last month.

mustKnowChunks.chunk: about 80% of feedback was against the proposal
mustKnowChunks.use: quantitative statistical clause indicating substantial public opposition
mustKnowChunks.example: Surveys revealed that about 80% of feedback was against the proposal to close the library.

sentenceAnalysis.mustKnowGrammar: Compound sentence joined by coordinating conjunction ('and'); first clause in present continuous ('Many residents are sharing their thoughts'); second clause with quantitative percentage subject ('about 80% of feedback during a consultation period') and prepositional complement ('was against the proposal').
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanation: The town asked citizens: 'What do you think of this idea?' / People spoke up loudly! / Eight out of every ten people said: 'No, we do not want this smartphone rule!'
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanationKo: 시에서 시민들에게 물었습니다: '이 아이디어에 대해 어떻게 생각하시나요?' / 시민들은 분명하게 목소리를 냈습니다! / 열 명 중 여덟 명이 이렇게 답한 것입니다: '아니요, 우리는 이런 스마트폰 규칙을 원치 않습니다!'

teachingTranscript.english: Look at the proportion in Sentence 6: 'about 80% of feedback during a consultation period was against the proposal.' That is four out of five responses opposing the guideline!
teachingTranscript.korean: 6번 문장의 비율을 보세요: '의견 수렴 기간 동안 피드백의 약 80%가 그 제안에 반대했습니다.' 5명 중 4명이 이 지침에 반대한 것입니다!

teachingTranscript.english: What does this tell us about the democratic process in Toyoake? Residents actively participate in public consultations and express strong dissent.
teachingTranscript.korean: 이것이 도요아케시의 민주적 절차에 대해 무엇을 말해주나요? 주민들이 공공 의견 수렴에 적극적으로 참여하고 강력한 반대 의사를 표현한다는 점입니다.

sentenceAnalysis.original: Some people worry that two hours isn’t enough for activities like reading or watching a movie.
sentenceAnalysis.chunkReading: Some people worry that / two hours isn’t enough / for activities / like reading or watching a movie.
sentenceAnalysis.directKorean: 어떤 사람들은 걱정합니다 / 2시간은 충분하지 않다고 / 활동들을 하기에 / 독서나 영화 감상과 같은.
sentenceAnalysis.naturalKorean: 어떤 이들은 독서나 영화 감상 같은 여가 활동을 즐기기에는 2시간이 턱없이 부족하다고 우려합니다.

mustKnowChunks.chunk: worry that two hours isn’t enough
mustKnowChunks.use: mental verb followed by that-clause stating a specific practical objection
mustKnowChunks.example: Commuters worry that thirty minutes isn’t enough time to catch the connecting train.

mustKnowChunks.chunk: for activities like reading or watching a movie
mustKnowChunks.use: prepositional phrase with examples illustrating culturally legitimate screen usage
mustKnowChunks.example: Tablets are commonly used for activities like reading or watching a movie during travel.

sentenceAnalysis.mustKnowGrammar: Indefinite plural subject ('Some people'); reporting/mental verb ('worry'); noun complement clause introduced by 'that' with singular duration subject ('two hours') taking singular contracted verb ('isn’t enough'); prepositional phrase specifying activities with coordinating gerunds ('reading or watching a movie').
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanation: A lot of folks said: 'Wait a second! A movie takes two full hours all by itself! / And what if I am reading an e-book on my tablet? / Two hours is just way too short for normal hobbies!'
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanationKo: 많은 사람들이 이렇게 말했습니다: '잠깐만요! 영화 한 편만 봐도 꼬박 2시간이 걸리잖아요! / 태블릿으로 전자책을 읽고 있다면 어떡하고요? / 평범한 취미 생활을 하기에도 2시간은 너무 짧습니다!'

teachingTranscript.english: Why do some residents oppose the two-hour limit? Because two hours isn't enough for activities like reading an e-book or watching a movie.
teachingTranscript.korean: 일부 주민들이 왜 2시간 제한에 반대하나요? 전자책을 읽거나 영화를 보는 등의 활동을 하기에 2시간이 충분하지 않기 때문입니다.

teachingTranscript.english: Notice the grammar of 'two hours isn't enough': a quantity of time is treated as a singular unit here.
teachingTranscript.korean: 'two hours isn't enough'의 문법에 주목하세요: 시간의 양은 여기서 단수 단위로 취급됩니다.

sentenceAnalysis.original: The mayor recognizes that while smartphones are useful, they can also lead to students missing school or families spending less time together.
sentenceAnalysis.chunkReading: The mayor recognizes that / while smartphones are useful, / they can also lead to / students missing school / or families spending less time together.
sentenceAnalysis.directKorean: 시장은 인정합니다 / 스마트폰이 유용하지만, / 그것들이 또한 초래할 수 있다는 점을 / 학생들이 학교를 결석하거나 / 가족들이 함께 보내는 시간이 줄어드는 것을.
sentenceAnalysis.naturalKorean: 시장은 스마트폰이 유용하다는 점을 인정하면서도, 한편으로는 학생들이 학교를 결석하게 되거나 가족들이 함께 보내는 시간이 줄어드는 결과로 이어질 수도 있다는 점을 짚고 있습니다.

mustKnowChunks.use: reporting verb introducing a concessive subordinate clause followed by the main assertion
mustKnowChunks.example: The principal recognizes that while digital tablets assist learning, they can also cause distraction.

mustKnowChunks.use: modal causal phrasal verb linking technology habits to negative social consequences
mustKnowChunks.example: Late-night gaming can also lead to students arriving exhausted at school.

mustKnowChunks.use: noun phrase with participle/gerund expressing chronic student absenteeism
mustKnowChunks.example: Officials expressed concern about students missing school due to unregulated internet addictions.

mustKnowChunks.meaning: 가족들이 함께 보내는 시간이 줄어드는 것
mustKnowChunks.use: noun phrase with participle describing weakened domestic communication and cohesion
mustKnowChunks.example: Silent dinner tables show families spending less time together in direct conversation.

sentenceAnalysis.mustKnowGrammar: Subject ('The mayor') followed by cognitive reporting verb ('recognizes'); complement clause introduced by 'that' containing a concessive dependent clause introduced by 'while' ('while smartphones are useful'); main clause with modal auxiliary ('can also lead to') governing two parallel gerund phrases with overt semantic subjects ('students missing school or families spending less time together').
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanation: The mayor says: 'Look, I know phones are super helpful in our daily lives. / But when kids stay up all night on screens, they miss school the next morning, / and parents and children stop having real conversations together.'
sentenceAnalysis.feynmanExplanationKo: 시장님은 이렇게 말합니다: '저도 휴대폰이 일상생활에서 매우 편리하다는 것을 잘 압니다. / 하지만 밤새 화면만 보다가 다음 날 학교를 결석하는 학생들이 생기고, / 부모와 자녀가 마주 보고 진솔한 대화를 나누는 시간이 점점 사라지고 있습니다.'

teachingTranscript.english: Examine the closing sentence: 'The mayor recognizes that while smartphones are useful, they can also lead to students missing school or families spending less time together.'
teachingTranscript.korean: 마지막 문장을 살펴보세요: '시장은 스마트폰이 유용하지만, 학생들이 학교를 결석하거나 가족들이 함께 보내는 시간이 줄어드는 결과로 이어질 수도 있다는 점을 인정합니다.'

teachingTranscript.english: Notice how 'while' balances both sides: phones are useful, but excessive use creates school absenteeism and weakens family bonds.
teachingTranscript.korean: 'while'이 어떻게 양면의 균형을 맞추는지 주목하세요: 휴대폰은 유용하지만, 과도한 사용은 학생 결석을 초래하고 가족 간의 유대를 약화시킵니다.
